LD 1025, An Act to Allow Federal Civil Service to Count for Purposes of Maine
Public Employees Retirement System Benefits

Good morning Senator Tipping, Chair Roeder and the other distinguished members of the Joint
Standing Committee on Labor. I am Bill Brown, Director of Actuarial and Legislative Affairs for
the Maine Public Employees Retirement System (MainePERS).
MainePERS is neither for nor against LD 1025. We are here to provide information and to offer
any assistance the committee may request surrounding this bill.

The State/Teacher Plan administered by MainePERS provides a defined benefit plan for State employees and teachers. Eligibility for a sen/ice retirement benefit and the amount of that benefit are determined in part by a member's years of sen/ice. Under limited circumstances members may purchase additional sen/ice credit to increase the total service credit used in the
calculation of benefits. A chart showing examples of the types of service credit currently eligible for purchase is attached to this testimony. Purchased service credit may allow a member to
retire earlier or with an increased retirement benefit.

LD 1025 proposes to allow a member of the State/Teacher Plan who previously sen/ed as an
employee of the federal employment service to purchase up to 5 years of service credit at
actuarial, or unsubsidized, cost.

There is no fiscal impact to LD 1025 as drafted. As a member opting to purchase service credit

under the provisions of LD 1025 isrequired to pay the full actuarial.

y

The bill as drafted does not afford members in the Participating Local District (PLD) Plan the same opportunity to purchase federal employment service as that being proposed for members of the State/Teacher Plan. Amending the bill to include this provision in the laws that govern
these plans would enable consistency in the laws regarding this specific provision.

Additionally, the phrase "federal employment service" is currently used in Title 5 to refer to a specific type of federal employment that can be included as service credit in the State/Teacher
Plan. We would be happy to work with the bill sponsor and the committee analyst to clarify the
language of the bill.

Thank you for your consideration of this testimony. l am happy to answer any questions and I
will be present for the work session.

Dear Members of the Committee on Labor,
I am writing to express my support for LD 1025, "An Act to Allow Federal Civil Service to
Count for Purposes of Maine Public Employees Retirement System Benefits."
This legislation is an important and necessary step In acknowledging the individuals who have dedicated portions of their careers to federal service, who wish to continue a career of
service within the State of Maine.

My career has been dedicated to public safety from the age of seventeen when I started
serving my local Volunteer Fire Department. Having sustained an injury that disqualified me from military service early in my public safety career, I chose to serve my country
through the Federal Service. I had the honor of serving within the Department of Homeland
Security -Transportation Security Administration for over 5 years at the Portland
International Jetport and the Bangor International Airport. Over that time, I had witnessed the dedication and expertise that ourfederal workers can bring to our State and Municipal
workforce.

Allowing the federal service time to count toward the Maine Public Employees Retirement System would benefit in enhancing recruitment and retention of skilled professionals with federal experience and give credit to those skilled professionals that have dedicated themselves to a career of civil service.
By passing LD 1025 Maine will be showing their support for federal employees who have
dedicated themselves to servingthe public and seek to continue their service at the State and Local level.
I respectfully request the Committee support LD 1025 and personally recommend its passage. Thank you for your consideration.

Very Respectfully submitted,

Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder and Distinguished Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Labor:
I am Matthew Harrington; and I represent Senate District 33, which includes the municipalities of
Alfred, Lebanon, Sanford and Waterboro. I am here today to introduce LD 1025, "An Act to Allow
Federal Civil Service to Count for Purposes of Maine Public Employees Retirement System Benefits."
I was contacted by a gentleman who shared with me that, as a former federal employee, he is not able to include those years of service towards his Maine Public Employees Retirement System (MEPERS) benefits. There are many opportunities to purchase other forms of civil service within MEPERS. I
hope this committee will consider this as one more option.
Given the opportunity to purchase service credit up to five years for the period of time served as an employee of the federal government, the State of Maine may very well gain qualified, dedicated
employees. This benefit, so to speak, could tip the scales for a potential staffer.
I understand Mr. Joshua Godard will be presenting testimony and I'm sure he could answer questions
about his specific situation.
I thank you for your time and attention and look forward to your thoughtful consideration of this
proposal.
